note: The OLG covers fleeing felon and probation/parole violator ineligibility on the 'SNAP Disqualifications and Sanctions' page and provides BEACON intake procedures on the 'Case Manager Responsibilities' page (asking when/where probation was imposed, when the crime was committed). However, the OLG simplifies the 'actively seeking' standard to a single scenario — law enforcement presents a felony arrest warrant with specific NCIC codes AND informs the state agency of intent to apprehend — whereas FNS 848.3 defines three distinct triggers: (1) law enforcement submits a request and states intent to enforce within 20 days, (2) law enforcement presents a felony arrest warrant, or (3) law enforcement states intent to enforce within 30 days of a state agency inquiry. The OLG collapses these into one combined requirement (warrant + intent), omitting the 20-day and 30-day timeframe distinctions and the scenario where the state agency initiates the inquiry. Additionally, the OLG does not address the FNS requirement that application processing must continue while awaiting verification of fleeing felon or probation/parole violator status, nor that the agency must process without consideration of that status if needed to meet processing time standards. The OLG also does not specify how to handle income and resources of members found ineligible under this provision (though general disqualified member budgeting rules may apply elsewhere). The 'contact the Procedural Issues mailbox' instruction suggests workers escalate rather than handle these cases themselves, which may explain the procedural gaps.
